Philosophy.pinyin: TÒNG ZÉ BÙ TŌNG, BÙ TŌNG ZÉ TÒNG
Philosophy.line1: Where there is pain, there is no free flow
Philosophy.line2: Where there is free flow, there is no pain
Philosophy.explanation: Within Traditional Chinese Medicine, discomfort or pain is among other things explained through disturbances in the free flow of Qi and blood. Acupuncture is traditionally aimed at supporting this flow and the body's natural balance.

Recognition.eyebrow: WHAT YOUR BODY IS ASKING FOR
Recognition.title: Symptoms do not always exist in isolation.
Recognition.paragraph1: Sometimes you know exactly what is bothering you. Sometimes you simply feel that your body is no longer responding as you would expect.
Recognition.paragraph2: Pain that keeps returning. A body that feels constantly tense. Poor sleep, low energy, or persistent complaints for which you have already tried various approaches.
Recognition.paragraph3: In Traditional Chinese Medicine, we do not look only at the complaint itself, but also at the whole picture.
Recognition.paragraph4: What may be contributing to the imbalance according to Traditional Chinese Medicine? And what does your body need to support its natural balance?
Recognition.intro1: Pain in your neck or back that keeps returning. Fatigue that does not disappear after a night's sleep. Or a lingering tension that you feel affects your mood, breathing, or sleep.
Recognition.intro2: Perhaps you have already tried various approaches, or have been told that you simply have to live with it. Yet you can often sense when something feels out of balance, and different complaints are not always completely separate.

pain.title: Recurring pain and tension
pain.description: Muscles that remain tight, recurring headaches, or joints that feel stiff. The worst peak may subside, but the body may never seem to fully relax.

energy.title: Persistent fatigue & stress
energy.description: You keep going through sheer determination, but daily life takes more effort than it used to. Mental restlessness, shallow breathing, or difficulty sleeping deeply.

unclear.title: Persistent, non-specific symptoms
unclear.description: Digestive complaints, hormonal fluctuations, or simply feeling less vital than usual. Conventional tests may show little, while you continue to notice that something does not feel right.

Recognition.bridgeTitle: Viewing the body as an interconnected whole
Recognition.bridgeText: Within Traditional Chinese Medicine, we do not only look at the area where you experience symptoms. We look at the whole picture and at the pattern that may be associated with your complaint according to TCM. We explore where the flow may be disturbed and what kind of support may be appropriate.

TreatmentMethod.title: Looking beyond the complaint.
TreatmentMethod.paragraph1: No two bodies are the same, and the same complaint can have a very different background from one person to another. That is why during the first appointment we take the time to understand your full story.
TreatmentMethod.paragraph2: We look not only at the symptom you are experiencing today, but also at your energy levels, sleep patterns, experienced tension, and lifestyle. This creates a broader picture of factors that may be connected to your concerns according to Traditional Chinese Medicine.
TreatmentMethod.paragraph3: Based on this TCM assessment, I create a personal treatment approach tailored to your needs and to what emerges during the consultation and treatment.

Help.title: What can you consult Bái Kāng for?

pain.title: Pain & tension

digestion.description: Digestive complaints such as bloating, abdominal discomfort, or an unsettled digestive system.

gender.title: Women & men

acupuncture.description: Every body tells its own story. Based on the principles of TCM, I look beyond the symptom itself and consider the whole person and the connections between different factors.
acupuncture.alt: Acupuncture treatment in a peaceful clinic room

laser.title: Modern technology, ancient wisdom
laser.description: Modern technology based on the principles of acupuncture. Laser acupuncture stimulates acupuncture points without needles and can be used when a needle-free treatment is appropriate.

LaserAcupuncture.title: Laser acupuncture: targeted and needle-free
LaserAcupuncture.paragraph1: For those who are sensitive to needles or prefer not to have traditional needles, laser acupuncture offers a needle-free treatment approach. Concentrated light is used to stimulate acupuncture points in a targeted way.
LaserAcupuncture.paragraph2: Within the clinic, laser acupuncture is used for, among other things, tension complaints, as support for pain complaints, and as support when quitting smoking.

Acupuncture.metaTitle: What is Acupuncture? | Traditional Chinese Medicine Tilburg | Bai Kang
Acupuncture.metaDescription: Discover acupuncture from the perspective of Traditional Chinese Medicine and modern physiology. Personal assessment, calm treatments, and laser acupuncture in Tilburg.
Acupuncture.heroIntro: Acupuncture has been used for thousands of years within Traditional Chinese Medicine. At Bai Kang, I look not only at the specific complaint, but at your situation as an interconnected whole.
Acupuncture.holisticTitle: Acupuncture is more than a needle on a point.
Acupuncture.holisticP1: A complaint rarely exists entirely on its own. Pain, tension, fatigue, or sleep problems can influence how you feel and respond in daily life. Within Traditional Chinese Medicine, we therefore look beyond the area where the discomfort appears.
Acupuncture.holisticP2: How does your body feel? How do you sleep? What is your energy level throughout the day? And how do different physical signals relate to one another?
Acupuncture.holisticP3: During treatment, I use these answers to form an individual treatment picture and to tailor the selection of acupuncture points accordingly.
Acupuncture.needleAlt: Detail of fine acupuncture needles on a stone
Acupuncture.modernTitle: A treatment that stimulates the body.
Acupuncture.modernIntro: Modern physiology studies how acupuncture may influence the nervous system, pain processing, and local tissue responses. Within TCM, this is viewed in terms of supporting the free flow of Qi and natural balance. These perspectives can exist alongside one another.
Acupuncture.visualAlt: Visualization of Body, Patterns, and Balance at Bai Kang TCM
Acupuncture.phase1Desc: Very fine, sterile needles provide a subtle stimulus at carefully selected points, based on your individual TCM assessment.
Acupuncture.phase2Desc: The body responds to the stimulation. From a modern physiological perspective, this includes responses of the nervous system and local tissue processes.
Acupuncture.phase3Desc: While resting on the treatment table, your body has time to respond to the treatment. Many people experience a deep sense of relaxation during this time.
Acupuncture.tcmTitle: The perspective of Traditional Chinese Medicine.
Acupuncture.tcmQuote: “The body is not viewed as a collection of separate parts, but as a dynamic whole.”
Acupuncture.qiDesc: Within TCM, the free circulation of Qi and blood is considered important for natural balance. Stagnation is traditionally associated with tension and pain complaints.
Acupuncture.balanceDesc: Within TCM, different bodily functions are considered interconnected. Factors such as sleep, nutrition, and daily demands may be related to how someone feels.
Acupuncture.diffDesc: Two people with the same headache may receive different treatment approaches within TCM because their findings and underlying patterns may differ.
Acupuncture.lifestyleDesc: Sleep, stress, nutrition, and daily demands are considered as part of the overall picture so that treatment can be tailored as closely as possible to your situation.
Acupuncture.complaintsIntro: Acupuncture is used in the clinic for a wide variety of concerns. The main areas of focus include:
Acupuncture.catPainDesc: Back, neck, and shoulder complaints, tension headaches, joint pain, and persistent muscular tension.
Acupuncture.catStressDesc: Difficulty relaxing, a busy mind, inner restlessness, and disrupted sleep.
Acupuncture.catEnergyDesc: Persistent fatigue, low energy, or difficulty recovering after physical exertion.
Acupuncture.catDigestionDesc: Bloating, stomach complaints, sluggish digestion, and abdominal cramps.
Acupuncture.catGenderDesc: Cycle-related complaints, menopausal symptoms, and emotional fluctuations.
Acupuncture.catSmokingDesc: Specific treatment programmes using laser acupuncture and auricular acupuncture as support when quitting smoking and vaping.
Acupuncture.ctaComplaints: View all specific indications on the complaints page
Acupuncture.step1Desc: We take the time to listen to your story. What is your concern? How did the complaints develop, and how do they affect your daily life?
Acupuncture.step2Desc: Through observation, tongue and pulse diagnosis, I form a TCM treatment picture and assess which pattern appears to be most prominent according to this approach.
Acupuncture.step3Desc: Very fine needles are carefully placed. You then rest for approximately 25 to 30 minutes in a quiet, warm treatment room.
Acupuncture.step4Desc: We discuss what you experienced and how your body responded. Follow-up treatments are adjusted according to your current response.
Acupuncture.relaxTitle: Lie quietly. Take a moment for yourself.
Acupuncture.relaxDesc: No screens. No hurry. The needles are so fine that insertion is often barely noticeable. What remains is a quiet moment in which your body has time to respond to the treatment.
Acupuncture.relaxAlt: Patient deeply relaxed during an acupuncture session
Acupuncture.laserTitle: Acupuncture does not always require needles.
Acupuncture.laserP1: For those who are sensitive to stimulation, feel apprehensive about traditional needles, or simply prefer a needle-free approach, laser acupuncture offers an alternative without needles.
Acupuncture.laserP2: Instead of needles, concentrated low-level light is used to stimulate the same acupuncture points without penetrating the skin.
Acupuncture.laserP3: At Bai Kang, laser acupuncture is used for tension complaints, as support for pain complaints, and as part of the targeted programme for quitting smoking and vaping.
Acupuncture.careDesc: Acupuncture is a complementary treatment approach and does not replace necessary conventional medical care. In acute or severe situations, conventional medical assessment is appropriate. At Bai Kang, I work with care, attention, and respect for conventional medical diagnostics.
Acupuncture.finalCtaTitle: Could acupuncture be suitable for your situation?
Acupuncture.finalCtaIntro: You do not need to know in advance which treatment approach you need. During an initial consultation, we discuss what is going on and consider together what may be appropriate.

metadata.title: My Approach & Method | Acupuncture Tilburg | Bai Kang TCM
metadata.description: Learn how treatment at Bai Kang TCM works, from the digital intake form and pulse diagnosis to acupuncture and careful evaluation.

hero.title: No standard treatment, but attention to your situation.
hero.intro: Every complaint is different. That is why treatment at Bai Kang does not begin with a fixed set of points or techniques, but with your story. Through Traditional Chinese Medicine, I look at your complaints, your body, and factors that may influence how you feel.

preparation.title: Prepare first, then explore further.
preparation.p1: Good care begins before you enter the clinic. After booking your appointment, you receive a digital intake form in which you can calmly describe your concerns, the course of your complaints, and relevant health history.
preparation.p2: Because I review your answers beforehand, we can use the consultation to focus directly on your situation. We look at the relationship between energy, sleep, nutrition, stress, and your concerns.
preparation.p3: Within Traditional Chinese Medicine, I combine this background with targeted pulse and tongue diagnosis. Based on these findings, I determine which treatment approach may be appropriate.
preparation.quote: “Not every complaint requires the same approach. And no two treatments need to be identical.”
preparation.imageAlt: Personal intake and attentive listening at Bai Kang TCM

steps.title: Your treatment step by step.
steps.subtitle: From preparation at your own pace to targeted care and regular evaluation.
steps.step1Desc: After booking your appointment, you receive an intake form by email. You can take your time to describe your complaints, medical background, and lifestyle. This allows me to prepare for your consultation.
steps.step2Desc: During the consultation, we take time to explore your answers. We look beyond the specific area of pain and consider the broader picture, including energy, tension, sleep, and lifestyle. Traditional observation and pulse diagnosis are used to form a TCM treatment picture.
steps.step3Desc: Following the intake, your first treatment takes place. Acupuncture forms the basis, optionally complemented by cupping or Guasha when appropriate within the treatment approach. The treatment is calm and tailored to your situation.
steps.step4Desc: During follow-up appointments, we discuss what has changed since the previous session in terms of pain, rest, or energy. The treatment approach adapts to your body's response; nothing is fixed permanently.

acupunctureBasis.title: Acupuncture as the foundation.
acupunctureBasis.p1: Classical acupuncture forms the heart of my practice in Tilburg. Very fine, sterile single-use needles are used to stimulate specific acupuncture points on the body.
acupunctureBasis.p2: The points selected are based on your intake form and the findings from the consultation and pulse diagnosis. The stimulation can produce local responses and responses from the nervous system. Many people experience relaxation during or after treatment.
acupunctureBasis.p3: When appropriate, this foundation can be complemented by supportive techniques to help release tension.
acupunctureBasis.imageAlt: Close-up of a very fine sterile acupuncture needle

additional.title: Complementary treatment methods.
additional.intro: Alongside acupuncture, supportive methods can be used to help address local muscular tension or support circulation.
additional.cuppingDesc: Glass or silicone cups are placed on the skin to create mild suction. Within TCM, this method is used among other things for tense or stiff muscles and as a complementary treatment approach.
additional.guashaDesc: Guasha involves gently scraping the oiled skin with a smooth instrument. Within TCM, this traditional technique is used as a complementary treatment for muscular tension and stiffness.
additional.laserDesc: When needles are not preferred or appropriate, laser acupuncture offers a needle-free treatment approach. At Bai Kang, laser acupuncture is also specifically used within the targeted programme for quitting smoking and vaping.

frequency.title: How often will you need treatment?
frequency.p1: This varies from person to person, depending on the nature of the complaint and how long it has been present. Some complaints may change relatively quickly, while longer-standing complaints can require more time. Individual responses to treatment also vary.
frequency.p2: That is why I deliberately do not make promises about a fixed number of sessions. During treatment, we observe how your body and complaints respond and discuss together which next step may be appropriate.
frequency.quote: No standard number of sessions, but a treatment path tailored to your individual process.

practical.title: Consultations & Coverage.
practical.subtitle: Clarity about treatment duration, preparation, and insurance coverage.
practical.firstDesc: Includes the completed digital intake form, personal consultation, traditional diagnostics, and the first acupuncture session.
practical.followDesc: A brief evaluation of your progress since the previous session, followed by a targeted treatment tailored to your situation.
practical.insuranceDesc: Acupuncture is partially reimbursed by many Dutch health insurers through supplementary insurance. As a CAT therapist, I operate within the applicable quality and complaints frameworks (GAT/Wkkgz). Check your policy for current conditions.

contraindications.title: When is acupuncture not suitable?
contraindications.p1: Acupuncture is a valuable treatment method, but it is not appropriate for every situation. In acute medical emergencies, high fever, or sudden unexplained pain, medical assessment should come first.
contraindications.p2: If you are receiving specialist medical treatment, we consider how TCM can support you in a safe and responsible way. During the first appointment, we therefore assess whether treatment is appropriate for your situation.

finalCta.title: Together, we look at what is appropriate.
finalCta.desc: You do not need to know exactly which technique or treatment you need beforehand. Tell me what you are dealing with, and from there we can calmly determine the appropriate approach.

Metadata.title: About Me | Patrick Witkamp | Acupuncture Tilburg | Bai Kang TCM
Metadata.description: Read the personal story of Patrick Witkamp. From more than 25 years in transport to Traditional Chinese Medicine, acupuncture, and laser therapy in Tilburg.

Hero.title: From the road to the treatment room.
Hero.lead: I am Patrick Witkamp, acupuncturist and owner of Bai Kang TCM in Tilburg. My path to Chinese medicine was anything but straightforward.
Hero.paragraph1: I was born on January 25, 1974, in Nijmegen, but spent my early childhood in Tunisia. My first years in North Africa unknowingly laid an important foundation for who I would later become. Travel, different cultures, and adapting to new situations became natural to me from an early age.
Hero.paragraph2: After returning to the Netherlands, I grew up in the Tilburg region. My career then took a very different direction from the treatment room.

Transition.title: A life that initially took a very different direction.

Journey.statLabel: Years in transport & on the road
Journey.statSub: From regional distribution to long-distance journeys and life in a mobile office.
Journey.title: More than 25 years on the road
Journey.p1: My career began in logistics, a world I knew from home through my father. After my logistics education, I eventually chose life on the road, in a mobile office. For more than twenty-five years I worked in transport, from regional distribution to long-distance journeys. It was a profession that gave me freedom and took me to many different places.
Journey.p2: That need for freedom and adventure also took me beyond the Netherlands. I lived and worked in Australia and Thailand. In Thailand, I met my partner Sompong. I worked there as an entrepreneur, in avionics, and taught English.
Journey.quote: For many years, my life took place outside the treatment room. Yet somewhere in the background there was always a fascination with something different.
Journey.p3: Life on the road and abroad shaped me: practical thinking, adapting quickly, and above all respecting every person's unique background.

Fascination.quote: For years, nothing came of it.
Fascination.p1: As a teenager, I saw a scene in a Steven Seagal film. After being injured during a fight, he was treated with acupuncture by an elderly Chinese monk. Afterwards, he entered a deep state of meditation.
Fascination.p2: It was just a film scene, but the image stayed with me. The small needles, the calm, and the idea that you could work with the body in such a simple way. Of course, I could not have known where that fascination would eventually lead.
Fascination.imageAlt: Acupuncture needles in a tranquil arrangement

Turnaround.title: The moment I decided to change direction
Turnaround.intro: After more than twenty-five years in transport, I read an article about a woman who, after thirty years at a well-known retail chain, decided to follow her heart and become an acupuncturist. Her story affected me deeply.
Turnaround.beforeText: Transport, long-distance journeys, international travel, entrepreneurship, and the practical dynamics of everyday life on the road.
Turnaround.afterText: Intensive study, Traditional Chinese Medicine, needle and laser techniques, and the calm of my own treatment room.

Timeline.title: My development step by step.
Timeline.subtitle: My journey from transport to acupuncture progressed step by step.
Timeline.step1Desc: After more than twenty-five years in transport, I decided to take a different path and seriously immerse myself in acupuncture and Traditional Chinese Medicine.
Timeline.step2Desc: My training began at Qing Bai with the Basic Professional Training.
Timeline.step3Desc: After obtaining my certificate, I moved to Total Health. There I completed the advanced year twice, followed by the final specialization year.
Timeline.step4Desc: At Qing Bai, I completed the Western Medical Foundations programme.
Timeline.step5Desc: In May 2026, I received my diplomas and completed an important stage in my development as an acupuncturist. For me, this does not mark the end of my education, but the beginning of a new chapter.

Craft.title: From interest to profession.
Craft.p1: During my training, I became increasingly interested in the way Chinese medicine looks at the body. Not only at the place where someone experiences complaints, but at the whole person and the relationship between different factors.
Craft.p2: That perspective still appeals to me. Not because every complaint has one simple explanation, but precisely because every person is different.

Vision.title: First the person, then the complaint.
Vision.lead: That may be the most important idea behind Bai Kang.
Vision.p1: When someone comes to me with a complaint, I do not want to immediately reach for a standard treatment. I first want to understand what someone is experiencing, how the complaint developed, and which circumstances may play a role.
Vision.p2: Traditional Chinese Medicine gives me its own way of looking at and assessing the body. From that perspective, I look for an approach that fits the person sitting in front of me. No fixed formula simply because someone has a particular complaint. A treatment that begins with the person.

Growth.title: Keep developing.
Growth.intro: My goal is not to use as many techniques as possible. My goal is to know when a particular approach may be appropriate.

Brand.title: A peaceful place for attention and treatment.
Brand.intro: Bai Kang is more than the name of my practice. It is where my different experiences come together.
Brand.baiDesc: The first sound refers to White, connecting it to my own name. Bái represents the clear, grounded, honest way in which I look at a complaint.
Brand.kangDesc: Kāng represents health and wellbeing. The name therefore creates a meaningful connection between my own name and the direction I have chosen for my practice.

CtaSection.quote: My path to acupuncture was not planned. Perhaps that is exactly why I find it important to approach every person without a fixed formula.
